guides.title: How to Brief the Faceless Channel Generator
guides.excerpt: Learn to prompt ShortDrafts for daily faceless content without revealing your identity.
guides.alt: Hands filming a product, no face on camera

sections.heading: What channels qualify?
paragraphs: Faceless channels let you post daily without showing your face. Think voiceover shorts, product demos, or text-driven narratives.
ShortDrafts generates batch ideas, hooks, and timed scripts tailored to these formats.
bullets: Voiceover narration over B-roll
Product unboxing or demonstration
Text-on-screen storytelling

sections.heading: How to write an effective brief?
paragraphs: Start with your niche and target audience. Specify video length, tone, and any recurring motifs.
Add constraints like ‘no face shown’ and ‘focus on hands or objects’ to keep the generator on track.
bullets: Niche: e.g., tech gadgets, cozy gaming
Length: 15–30 seconds
Tone: casual, informative, or dramatic

sections.heading: Where to generate and export?
paragraphs: Open the ShortDrafts interface and paste your brief. The tool returns a complete package ready for editing.
To start a new project, go to the generate page in plain words—just type the URL ending in generate.html into your browser.

guides.title: What is an AI Shorts content generator?
guides.excerpt: One topic in. Ideas, hooks, a spoken script, titles, and captions out.
guides.alt: A marked-up script on a wooden desk

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: It is a writing tool. You type a topic, pick a platform, a style, and a length, and it returns a content pack you can speak, type on screen, and paste under a post.
It is not a video renderer. There is no MP4 at the end of the run.

sections.heading: What is in a pack
paragraphs: A pack is the words around one idea, written for a 15–60 second clip.
bullets: A few distinct angles so you can pick one
Hooks written for the first three seconds
A timed spoken script
Title options, a caption, a CTA, and on-screen lines

sections.heading: Who it is for
paragraphs: People who still shoot their own clips — talking head, B-roll, or a faceless voiceover. If you wanted an avatar studio, this is the wrong tab.

guides.title: Do I get a finished YouTube Short video?
guides.excerpt: No. You get the writing layer. The camera, the cut, and the post are still yours.
guides.alt: A camera on a tripod waiting to shoot

sections.heading: What you walk away with
paragraphs: A pack of copy. You can read the script into a mic, put the on-screen lines over B-roll, and paste a title and caption when you upload.

sections.heading: What this site will not do
paragraphs: It will not stitch stock footage, clone a voice, or export a file you can upload as-is. If you need a video model or an editor, copy the words and use those tools after.
bullets: No finished MP4
No avatar or fake studio
No promise that a pack goes viral

sections.heading: A clean stop line
paragraphs: If a claim would need a lawyer, a lab, or a licensed trade, it does not belong in a 30-second script here. The generator writes words. You decide what is safe to say on camera.

guides.title: Can I make faceless Shorts with this?
guides.excerpt: Yes. Pick the faceless style for a voiceover draft and lines that work without your face.
guides.alt: Hands filming a product, no face on camera

sections.heading: What faceless means here
paragraphs: You stay off camera. The pack is written to be heard and read: a voiceover script, on-screen text, and titles that still stop a thumb without a talking head.

sections.heading: How to generate one
paragraphs: On the generate page, set style to faceless. Keep the topic concrete — a product, a niche, or a single claim you can show with B-roll.
bullets: Read the script into a mic, or drop it into a voice tool you already use
Lay the on-screen lines over screen recordings, hands, or stock you have rights to
Use a title and caption tuned to Shorts, TikTok, or Reels

sections.heading: What still has to be yours
paragraphs: Footage, voice, and the edit. The pack does not pick clips or license music. It only writes the words so the shoot has a spine.

guides.title: Which platforms does it support?
guides.excerpt: YouTube Shorts, TikTok, and Instagram Reels — same idea, copy tuned to the app you post in.
guides.alt: Three phones showing different vertical clips

sections.heading: What changes per platform
paragraphs: The idea can stay the same. Titles, captions, and hashtags shift so they sound native to the app you pick, not copied from another feed.

sections.heading: What does not change
paragraphs: A pack is still a writing pack. You still shoot or assemble the clip. Algorithm tricks, bought views, and “guaranteed viral” language are not in scope.
bullets: YouTube Shorts
TikTok
Instagram Reels

sections.heading: If you post in more than one place
paragraphs: Generate once per platform if you want the caption and hashtags retuned. Do not treat one caption as interchangeable across all three.

guides.title: Is it free?
guides.excerpt: Yes. Ten packs a day, no login, no credit card, no paid plan behind the button.
guides.alt: A laptop and coffee on a cafe table

sections.heading: What “free” means
paragraphs: The generator is free to use. There is no Creator or Pro tier, and this site does not run ads on these pages.

sections.heading: The daily cap
paragraphs: You get 10 content packs per day, counted by IP address. Regenerating a pack counts as a run. The cap exists so hosting stays up, not to upsell a paid plan.
bullets: No account required
No credit card
The limit resets on the calendar day

sections.heading: If you hit the wall
paragraphs: Wait for the next day, or email contact@shortdrafts.com if a run failed and you think the count is wrong. Include the topic and about what time it happened.

guides.title: Why every pack leads with hooks
guides.excerpt: The first three seconds are the job. Slow intros get skipped.
guides.alt: A thumb pausing on a vertical video

sections.heading: The three rules
paragraphs: A Short lives or dies before the viewer decides to stay. Packs are written that way on purpose.
bullets: Open on a claim, a tension, or a picture — not a greeting
Make the next line earn the last one
Land a CTA that a real person would actually say

sections.heading: What you are working with
paragraphs: Each pack includes several hook options so you can test more than one cold open on the same idea. If a hook feels like a clickbait lie, skip it. The rest of the script should still make sense without it.

sections.heading: After you pick a hook
paragraphs: Read the full script out loud. If you cannot say it in one breath-friendly pass, cut it before you shoot. The generator drafts. You keep the final line.

guides.title: How to turn a pack into a Short
guides.excerpt: Generate, pick one angle, shoot or voice it, then paste the title and caption.
guides.alt: A creator speaking to a phone on a tripod

sections.heading: Before you generate
paragraphs: Come in with one topic you can show. “Morning routine for nurses” works. “Make me famous” does not.

sections.heading: The pass
bullets: Open generate and enter the topic
Pick Shorts, TikTok, or Reels
Choose talking-head or faceless, then a length
Generate, then pick one idea and one hook — not all of them

sections.heading: Then leave this site
paragraphs: Shoot, voice, or edit in the tools you already use. Come back only if you need another angle or a retune for a second platform.
If a generate run fails, use the contact page and include the topic and the time.
